tasks.title: Define Run-scoped client-authorized artifact ingress
tasks.objective: Freeze the smallest host-local capability, ownership, retry, resource and lifecycle contract for explicitly supplied opaque bytes beside one live native Run.
tasks.outcome: Clients can reason about authorization, Run scope, operation disposition and cleanup without introducing clipboard, Agent, SSH-deployment, Backend fallback or a second context identity into ctxmux.
acceptance: A reviewed ADR defines ArtifactId, exact target RunId, logical-name handling, RunHostPath/reference semantics, capability discovery, operation key, committed/failed/unknown disposition, lease, release, TTL, Run-terminal cleanup and daemon-start cleanup.
The caller alone decides whether clipboard, drag/drop, file or generated bytes may be shared; ctxmux never reads or infers source policy and daemon limits cannot be disabled by caller authorization.

Placement is daemon-host local: ctxmux chooses the physical destination beside the target Run and does not deploy over SSH, accept a client destination, transfer across Runs/hosts, or expose a remote-filesystem abstraction.
Artifact stage, ordinary Run input and release remain separate operations with separate correlated outcomes; no stage receipt claims that the Run or an Agent consumed the bytes.

The trust boundary covers same-UID exposure, path safety, permissions, quotas, misleading names, partial upload, disconnect, response loss, conflicting operation-key reuse, terminal-state Run, unsupported Backend and restart cleanup.
No Agent identity, message, permission, image decoding, prompt, UI or workspace policy enters foundational protocol types.

verification.proves: Owner, host locality, retry disposition, capability, resource, security, lifecycle and non-goal boundaries are reviewed before implementation.
Architecture links, wrong-case mappings and ordinary repository gates pass.

tasks.title: Implement bounded idempotent native-Run staging
tasks.objective: Implement the approved public protocol and daemon owner with bounded streaming, operation-status recovery, atomic exact-byte publication and race-safe cleanup for live native Runs.
tasks.outcome: A public client can recover a lost commit response without duplicate files, while every known failure publishes nothing and every committed artifact remains bounded and attributable to one Run.
acceptance: The Rust protocol SSOT defines capability, begin/chunk/commit/status/release frames, bounded identities, declared length/digest and generated TypeScript parity without placing a multi-megabyte artifact in one NDJSON frame or creating a general transaction bus.

The same operation key with identical RunId and content converges on one receipt; conflicting reuse fails. A lost success response is queryable during the documented daemon epoch, and SDKs do not retransmit uncertain bytes blindly.

The daemon validates a live native Run before consuming chunks, chooses an owner-only directory and create-new temporary file, rejects client destinations and unsafe names, verifies exact length/digest, and atomically publishes before success.
Per-upload, per-Run, concurrent and aggregate quotas bound memory, disk, descriptors and tasks; slow upload backpressure cannot starve status, cancellation, release, stop or shutdown.

Pre-commit cancellation, malformed frames, timeout, disconnect, digest mismatch and quota failure leave no ArtifactId, file, descriptor, task or charge. Commit, release, TTL/eviction, Run-terminal cleanup and startup cleanup share one lease-aware owner policy.
Exited/interrupted/missing Runs, imported tmux Runs, unsupported Backends and capability mismatch reject before bytes or filesystem mutation; artifacts never migrate to a Provider-resumed new RunId.

verification.proves: Protocol generation, TypeScript parity, operation idempotency, response loss, parser bounds, filesystem atomicity, quotas, cleanup and Run lifecycle regressions pass.
Upload, status, commit, release, retry lifetime, capability and unsupported semantics match the implementation.

tasks.title: Expose public artifact composition without host policy
tasks.objective: Expose staging, status, input composition and release to clean Rust, TypeScript and CLI consumers while keeping consent, SSH deployment and Agent UX in embedding hosts.
tasks.outcome: AgentMux and other clients can use one public boundary on whichever host's ctxmuxd they reach, with no private daemon access, destination path or image-specific API.
acceptance: Rust and @ctxmux/sdk expose streamed file/bytes, operation status, committed ArtifactId and RunHostPath/reference, cancellation, release and typed errors with bounded buffering through the public protocol only.

The CLI offers an explicit file-to-live-Run staging command with size, digest, identity, target Run, materialized reference and lifetime; it never reads clipboard state or uploads merely because attach starts.

A composition helper may stage then send the reference through correlated input, but stage, input and release results remain distinct so unknown input is not replayed and commit truth is not rewritten.

Documentation states that the receiving ctxmuxd stages on its own host. AgentMux may reach a remote ctxmuxd through an authenticated forward, but ctxmux owns no SSH install, credential or connection policy.
A clean TypeScript consumer stages authorized PNG and arbitrary fragmented binary data, sends the path to a shell Run and proves exact digest; a denial fixture issues no request and creates no file.
Examples contain no Agent, clipboard, Electron, React or conversation API and do not bypass Backend capability checks.

verification.proves: Rust, CLI, TypeScript, clean-consumer, exact-byte, denial, stage/input separation and repository regressions pass.
Generic composition, host locality, caller-owned policy, receipts, limits, cleanup and unsupported behavior are documented.

tasks.title: Qualify artifact ingress under hostile lifecycle and load
tasks.objective: Prove the complete public artifact contract under adversarial bytes, filesystem races, uncertain responses, disconnects, Run replacement, quotas, cleanup, restarts, concurrency and resource pressure.
tasks.outcome: Artifact ingress has no silent partial publication, duplicate commit, leaked file, resource escape, unsafe retry, cross-Run reuse, unsupported fallback or image-specific shortcut.
acceptance: Deterministic tests cover every frame boundary, arbitrary bytes, invalid metadata, traversal/symlink/replacement attempts, duplicate/conflicting operation keys, length/digest mismatch, late frames, cancellation, timeout, disconnect before/after commit, status query and release races.

Real filesystem fixtures prove private modes, atomic visibility, exact bytes, no partial reads or orphan temporaries, lease-safe explicit release, TTL/quota eviction, Run-terminal cleanup and startup cleanup on every supported local platform.

Stress lanes cover many Runs/uploads, slow/silent clients, aggregate exhaustion, shutdown and repeated cancellation with bounded RSS, descriptors, tasks, disk and latency and no control-path starvation.
A Run replacement fixture proves an artifact never crosses RunId; the new Run must stage independently. Imported tmux, terminal-state and unknown-capability targets fail before upload.
Security review confirms no clipboard reads, client physical destination, hidden remote transport, path disclosure through unrelated Runs, or stronger same-UID isolation claim.
Clean public-boundary qualification and documentation contain no silent fallback; unknown operation disposition remains explicit when its documented query lifetime is unavailable.

verification.proves: Protocol, lifecycle, chaos, stress, security, resource, cleanup, SDK, CLI and clean-consumer lanes pass together.
Every invariant, platform, resource result, unsupported capability and residual risk is auditable.
